subject: Islamic And Moral Studies
question: In the annual sports of school, 'A' stood second in race. But he told his friends that he secured 1st position. On the other hand, his elder brother enjoys handsome salary and facilities as a manager of a company. At this, most often he says, "Indeed, my company gives best livelihood to me."
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Iman?","marks":1,"answer":"Iman is to belief in the laws and regulations of Islamic Shariat at heart, to confess in words and to demonstrate in practice."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"\"Surely, to Allah the only code of life for mankind is Islam\". — Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Islam is the only religion or way of life chosen by Allah the Most High. Allah the Most High has sent many commands and regulations for the guidance of mankind throughout the ages. These commands and prohibitions have been given as Shariat. The final and perfect shape of Shariat is Islam. It is the final and best prescription of life directed to mankind. This is the religion acceptable to Allah the Most High. Allah the Most High says about this, \"Surely, to Allah the only code of life for mankind is Islam.\" (Sura Al-i-Imran, Ayat 19)."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which side of Aqaid has been demonstrated in the behaviour of 'A'? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Nifaq, one of the aspects of 'Aqaid', is revealed in A's behavior. The literal meaning of the word Nifaq is hypocrisy, duplicity, deception, etc. In terms of Shariah, accepting Islam with the mouth while hiding disbelief and disobedience in the heart is called Nifaq. Which is noticeable in the behavior of 'A'. 'A' from the stem secured 2nd position in running in the annual sports competition at the school. But he tells his friends he has secured the first position. His hypocrisy has been revealed in this action. Because, the Prophet (Sm.) has described the signs of hypocrites and said, \"A Munafiq has three distinctive marks. When he speaks he tells a lie, when he promises he breaks it, and when something is kept in his custody he grabs it.\" (Sahih Al-Bukhari) And since 'A' has lied to his friends that he has become first, he is committing Nifaq. Therefore, it can be said that 'A's behavior has manifested Nifaq."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Evaluate the speech of elder brother of 'A' in the light of the relevant topic of Aqaid.","marks":4,"answer":"The statement of A's elder brother is included in Shirk, which is a very heinous crime. Shirk means partnering. In Islamic terms, Shirk is the associating of a person or thing with Allah Almighty. Shirk is a very heinous crime. Shirk is the greatest oppression of all the oppressions in the world, which is revealed in the statement of the elder brother of 'A'. The elder brother 'A' from the stem is a manager of a company getting good salary and various benefits. Thus, he often said, \"Indeed, my company gives best livelihood to me.\" This is Shirk. Verily, Allah is our Creator and Sustainer. We enjoy His blessings. Even then, if anyone associates anything with Allah, then it is a greater injustice like no other. For this reason, Allah says, 'Verily, shirk is the extreme tyranny.' (Surah Luqman, verse 13) Allah is very displeased with the polytheists. He does not forgive the sin of polytheism, even though He is infinitely merciful. (Surah An-Nisa, verse 48) It is not possible to obtain the welfare of this world and the hereafter without the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. Allah says, \"Allah will certainly make paradise forbidden for the polytheists. In fact, his abode is hell.\" (Surah Al-Maida, verse 72) Therefore, shirk is an unforgivable crime. Finally, the statement of A's elder brother is an unforgivable offense as it involves shirk. And we should all stay away from such heinous crimes.\n---"}]

subject: Islamic And Moral Studies
question: Mr. 'Ka' went to a 'Mazar' of a peer before his exam and slaughtered a goat by the name of the peer and prayed for better result in exam. His friend 'Kha' became addicted when he went to Europe for his studies. After returning back one night his mother saw him drinking and told your work is not correct. In reply Mr. 'Kha' told, I think there is nothing wrong in it.
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called Nifaq?","marks":1,"answer":"Nifaq is showing outward allegiance by hiding the opposition of the mind."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is it important to believe in Akhirat? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Belief in Akhirat is important as it is the fundamental matter of Iman. The life after death of a human is called Akhirat. In the Akhirat, man will be held accountable for every act of his worldly life. Therefore, belief in the Akhirat prevents people from committing sins and encourages them to do good deeds. Besides, no one can be a true believer without belief in the Akhirat. For these reasons, it is important for a Muslim to belief in the Akhirat."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which matter is reflected by the activities of Mr. 'Ka'? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Shirk is reflected in Mr. Ka's activities. The word Shirk means associating partners. In Islamic terms, equating a person or thing with Almighty Allah is called shirk. Shirk is the opposite of Tawhid. Shirk with Allah can be of four types. One of them is associating someone with Allah in worship. For example, prostrating to someone other than Allah, slaughtering animals in someone's name, etc. Mr. 'Ka' has done such activities. From the above stem, Mr. 'Ka' slaughters a goat in the name of Mazar Pir in the hope of good results in the examination. This act of his includes shirk in the worship of Allah. Consequently, Mr. 'Ka' has to suffer severe punishment as a mushrik. In fact, shirk is a very heinous crime. Shirk is the biggest oppression in the world. Allah Ta'ala says: 'Verily, shirk is the extreme tyranny.' (Surah Luqman, verse 13) Allah is very displeased with the polytheists. He does not forgive the crime of shirk, despite being the Most Forgiving and the Most Merciful. Allah Ta'ala says - \"Surely, Allah will not forgive the sin of Shirk. Besides Shirk, He may forgive any other sin of whom He so desires.\" (Sura: An-Nisa, Ayat: 48) In the Akhirat, there is a painful punishment for the Muslims. It is clearly stated in Al-Quran, \"Allah will certainly make paradise forbidden for the polytheists. In fact, his abode is hell.\" (Sura: Al-Maida, Ayat: 72)"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the consequence of the activities of Mr. 'Kha' after identifying it.","marks":4,"answer":"The activities of Mr. 'Kha' have manifested kufr, the consequences of which are dire. Kufr means to deny, to disbelieve, to cover up, to conceal, to express ingratitude, to disobey, etc. Kufr is the opposite of Iman. Mr. 'Kha' does not consider drinking alcohol as wrong, which is considering haram as halal. In Islamic terms, disbelief in any of the fundamentals of Islam, the religion chosen by Allah Ta'ala, is called kufr. For example, considering haram as halal. We know that taking and dealing in narcotic drugs is haram. But Mr. 'Kha' accepted it as halal and committed blasphemy. Such actions breed disobedience and ingratitude in people. A disbeliever can freely disobey Allah's prohibitions as he denies His blessings. Allah Ta'ala says, \"Those who disbelieve and reject our signs will surely abide in hell. They will remain there forever.\" (Sura: Al-Baqara, verse: 39) From the above discussion,\n---"}]

subject: Islamic And Moral Studies
question: Shefali Begum was discussing with her friend Jhoma Begum about the subjects of Islam. Shefali Begum said that all the rules and regulations of Islam are acceptable to me though, but faith in Akhirat is not acceptable to me. I believe that the reward and punishment will be given in this world. In reply, Jhoma Begum told her that Islam is the religion of Allah and denying any one of its rules is kufr.
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Asmani Kitab?","marks":1,"answer":"All the books that Allah Ta'ala has sent down as guidance for mankind are called Asmani kitab."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"What do you understand by Risalat?","marks":2,"answer":"One of the fundamentals of Iman is belief in the Messengers or Prophets. The literal meaning of the word Risalat is to deliver a message, a letter, news, or to carry out a good deed. In Islamic terms, the responsibility of conveying the Holy Message of Almighty Allah to the people is called Risalat. And the one who fulfills this duty is called Rasul."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Describe the consequences of Shefali Begum's concept in light of your text book.","marks":3,"answer":"Shefali Begum's way of thinking revealed disbelief in the Akhirat, which has dire consequences. Akhirat means hereafter. The life after death is called Akhirat. Akhirat is eternal life. This is the permanent abode of man. Without belief in the Akhirat, people cannot be believers and Muttaki. But Shefali Begum's words disrupted this belief. Shefali Begum, from the stem, believes in all other laws of Islam but does not believe in the hereafter. But believing in the Akhirat is one of the things of Iman. If people do not believe in the Akhirat, they are not afraid of accountability in the Hereafter. As a result, they indulge in various kinds of vices. And for this, they will have to suffer severe punishment in the Akhirat. About this, Allah Ta'ala says, \"And if one disbelieves in Allah, His Angels, His Scriptures, His Prophets and the Last Day, one will deplorably go astray.\" (Sura: An-Nisa, Ayat: 136) Consequently, Shefali Begum will have to face a terrible fate for disbelieving in the Akhirat."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Is the remark of Jhoma Begum correct? Give logic in favour of your answer.","marks":4,"answer":"If one denies any of the rules of Islam, he/she will be considered a kafir - Jhoma Begum's remark is correct. Kufr literally means to deny, to disbelieve. Covering, concealing, disobeying, etc. Kufr is the opposite of Iman. Faith in the fundamentals of Islam is called Iman. And the Hereafter is one of the fundamentals of Islam. Therefore, disbelief in the Akhirat is also part of kufr, which is revealed in Jhoma Begum's statement. Shefali Begum doesn't believe in the Akhirat, according to the stem. Jhoma Begum commented on this act of hers as part of kufr, which is correct and reasonable. Because the hereafter is one of the fundamental issues of Islam. This is eternal life. This life has a beginning, but no end. In the Akhirat, people's actions in this world will be accounted for. Then there will be paradise as a reward for good deeds and hell as punishment for bad deeds. Shefali Begum does not believe in these things related to the Akhirat. Therefore, her belief is part of kufr. Hence, it can be said that denying any of the provisions of Islam is part of kufr. Thus, Jhoma Begum's statement in this regard is correct.\n---"}]

question: Mr. 'A' disbelieves some issues of Islam inspire of being a Muslim. On the other hand, Mr. 'B' has lent five thousand taka to his friend in condition of returning within three months. But his friend has not returned the money timely inspite of having ability. It has created dispute between both of them. In perspective of his friend's character, Imam said, "If he can not abandon this type of character, he will have to face severe punishment in Akhirat."
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Risalat?","marks":1,"answer":"The responsibility of conveying the holy message of Almighty Allah to people is called Risalat."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is the belief in Taqdir important? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Belief in Taqdir is important as it is one of the seven fundamentals of Iman. The word Taqdir means destiny, fate, or destiny. Almighty Allah is the sole decider of human destiny. Everything good and bad is determined by Him. People can achieve success in their work. But it is not possible without the grace of Almighty Allah. Allah Taala is the controller of all the success, failure, danger, and trouble of human life. It is not possible to be a believer without faith in destiny. Therefore, it is important to belief in Taqdir."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which thing is exposed in the character of Mr. 'A'? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Kufr has been manifested in the behavior of Mr. 'A', the consequences of which are dire in this life and the Akhirat. The word kufr means denial, disbelief, concealment, etc. In Islamic terms, disbelief in any of the fundamentals of Islam, the chosen deen of Allah Taala, is called kufr. Kufr is the opposite of Iman, which is also observed in the attitude of Mr. 'A'. It can be seen from the above stem that although Mr. 'A' is a Muslim, he does not believe in some of the fundamentals of Islam. His attitude is called kufr because disbelief in any of the seven aspects of Iman or Islam is tantamount to kufr. And the consequences of disbelief are very terrible. As a result, not only in the world; rather, people will have to accept a miserable end in the Hereafter. Kufr leads to immorality in personal and social life. Due to a lack of belief in the Hereafter, the morals of the disbelieving person deteriorate, and he indulges in various kinds of sins and immoral activities for the sake of this world. A kaffir person disbelieves in Allah Ta'ala and destiny. As a result, he becomes impatient and depressed at everything. Moreover, the consequences of disbelief in the Hereafter will be the painful punishment of Hell. About this, Allah Ta'ala says, 'Those who disbelieve and reject our signs will surely abide in hell. They will remain there forever.' (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 39) Therefore, it can be said that the result of kufr is nothing but destruction. We have to refrain from this."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Justify the statement of the respected Imam in perspective of the character of Mr. 'B's friend.","marks":4,"answer":"The behavior of Mr. 'B's friend revealed the characteristics of a Munafiq. Imam's statement in this context is correct. In general, those who keep a certain feeling in their hearts and express the opposite state outside are called hypocrites. Rasul (Sm.) mentioned the three characteristics of a Munafiq and said, \"A Munafiq has three distinctive marks. When he speaks, he tells a lie, when he promises he breaks it, and when something is kept in his custody, he grabs it.\" (Sahih Al-Bukhari). The behavior of Mr. 'B's friend is characterized by breach of promise. In the above stem, Mr. 'B' has lent five thousand taka to his friend in condition of returning within three months. But his friend has not returned the money timely inspite of having ability. It has created dispute between both of them. In perspective of his friend's character, Imam said, if he can not abandon this type of character, he will have to face sever punishment in Akhirat. Imam's statement about Nifaq is correct because adultery is a very heinous sin. It destroys human character and morality. As a result, people get used to lying. No one believes in hypocrites. Everyone looks at them with suspicion and hatred. They spend their lives being humiliated and insulted by the people of society. There is a very dire consequence for them in this life as well as in the hereafter. About this, Allah Ta'ala says, \"Surely the hypocrites will remain in the lowest layer of hell.\" (Sura An-Nisa, Ayat: 145). The above discussion proves that Mr. A friend of 'B' breaks his promise and reflected the characteristics of Munafiq, which are harmful to both this world and the Akhirat. And Imam's statement about this is correct.\n---"}]

subject: Islamic And Moral Studies
question: Murtuza believes that all the people of the world will one day face accountability to the creator for their activities. At the end of accounting, the virtuous will be rewarded with comfortable place and the sinners will be given a place of extreme punishment. That life has a beginning but no end. On the other hand, Kalim Miyan's idea is that since people will continue to come to the world until the doomsday, Allah will also send prophets to show the people the right path. He thinks that the chain of prophethood is still running.
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Tawhid?","marks":1,"answer":"Tawhid refers to the acceptance of Allah Almighty as One and Only entity."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"\"Man is the best creation among the all creatures.\" — Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Man is the best creation among the all creatures because his character, characteristics and activities are superior to other creatures. Humans are sentient beings. Humans are different from other animals because of conscience. Humans have special thinking power, creativity, which encourages them to do unique work. Hence human activities become idealized and improved. For these reasons man is called the best creature in creation."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"In the opinion of Kalim Miyan, which aspect of Islam is disbelieved? Explain the aspect.","marks":3,"answer":"Kalim Miyan's concept shows disbelief in Khatamun Nabuwwat. Khatamun Nabuwwat means the end of Prophethood. Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) was the last prophet. Through him, the completeness of the Deen has been declared. This idea is the essence of Khatamun Nabuwwat. Kalim Miyan's statement contradicts this. Kalim Miyan thinks that since people will continue to come to the world until the doomsday, Allah will also send prophets to show the people the right path. He thinks that the chain of prophethood is still running. Such statements are completely idle or false. Because, after the Holy Prophet (Sm.), no other Prophet-Messenger will come. Allah Ta'ala says, \"He is not the father of any of your males, rather is the Messenger of Allah and the last Prophet.\" (Sura: Al-Ahzab, Ayat: 40) And he is the Prophet of all people until the Day of Resurrection. His teaching is sufficient for all people. About this, Rasul (Sm.) himself said, \"I am the seal of the Prophets and after me there is no Prophet.\" (Sahih Muslim) Therefore, there is no need for any more Prophet-Messenger to come. Belief in this matter is belief in Khatamun Nabuwwat. And this belief is one of the parts of Iman. Disbelief in these leads people astray and astray. As a result, human life will end in failure."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Identify Murtuza's believe and analyze its impact on human life.","marks":4,"answer":"Murtuza's believe, i.e., believe in the Akhirat, has a great impact on human life. Akhirat means the hereafter. The life after human death is called Akhirat. The life of the hereafter has a beginning but no end. In this life, people will have to answer to Allah for their actions and will enjoy the results accordingly. And this belief is revealed in Murtuza's believe. Murtuza from the above step believes that all the people of the world will be accountable to the creator one day. On that day, the righteous will be given a place of comfort and the sinners a place of severe punishment. His belief in the Hereafter is revealed in this idea. The influence of belief in the Hereafter on human life is immense. In the Akhirat, all the actions of people will be accounted for. Then according to deeds, some will achieve great success, while others will suffer painful punishment. Therefore, in the afterlife, people should be motivated to do good deeds by renouncing all kinds of wrong and immoral actions to achieve great success and escape punishment, and to build a beautiful and moral life to attain Paradise, a place of eternal happiness. Therefore, it can be said that believe in the Hereafter encourages people to do good deeds and prevents them from doing wrong deeds. Hence, we have to have fear in our hearts about the Hereafter and follow Islamic law perfectly.\n---"}]

subject: Islamic And Moral Studies
question: Mr. Abdur Rahim discusses in his class, Allah has sent some greatest person to show the right path to those people who are going to astray. On the other hand, Mr. Rifat told to his students, there is a stage in the life hereafter where the people wait for the judgement of Allah. In that situation, judgement will be started by the request of Hazrat Muhammad (Sm.). Tomal, a student of that class told, the request of Hazrat Muhammad (Sm.) of that day is the special favour for the Muslim and Mumin.
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is called Sirat?","marks":1,"answer":"Sirat is a dark bridge installed over Hell from Hashr Maidan to Jannat."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is Al-Quran called \"An-Noor\"? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Al-Quran is called An-Noor because it is a light to guide people. An-Noor means light. Al-Quran is the light given by Allah to walk on the right path. About this, Allah Ta'ala says, \"And those who are with him, those who follow the light that has been revealed, they are the successful ones.\" (Sura Bani-Isra'il, Ayat 81)"},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which subject of Aqaid is reflected by the discussion of Mr. Abdur Rahim? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"Mr. Abdur Rahim's discussion reflected the identity of Risalat, one of the aspects of Aqaid. Risalat means message, letter, etc. The responsibility of conveying the Holy Message of Almighty Allah to people is called Risalat. The one who carries out the responsibility of Risalat is called Rasul. Allah Ta'ala has sent many prophets and messengers to the world throughout the ages. They called people to the true and beautiful path, which Mr. Abdur Rahim also revealed in his discussion. In the above stem, the identity of Risalat is found in Rahim's statement. Prophets and Messengers used to call people to the worship of Allah Ta'ala while carrying out their mission duties. He called them to the true and beautiful path. They used to guide the wayward people to find the right path to implement the laws of Allah Ta'ala on earth. Therefore, it can be said, Mr. Abdur Rahim's discussion reflected the identity of Risalat."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Evaluate the opinion of Tomal after identifying the discussing matter of Mr. Rifat.","marks":4,"answer":"Mr. Rifat's discussion and Tomal's opinion reflect the idea of Hashr and the Shafaat respectively. Hashr is a great gathering. One day all people from the beginning to the end of the world will gather in one place. This gathering of people is called Hashr. All human actions will be taken into account in Hashr Maidan, which is noticeable in Mr. Rifat's discussion. In the above stem, Mr. Rifat's statement refers to Hashr. On the other hand, Tomal, a student of that class, said that the Prophet's request on that day was a special blessing for Muslims and believers. In this statement of Tomal, the identity of intercession is found. Because what can be a greater blessing than the intercession of the Holy Prophet (Sm.) on the field of Hashr. On that day, no one will enter Paradise without the intercession of the Holy Prophet (Sm.). The Prophet (Sm.) said, \"I have been granted the right to make recommendations.\" (Sahih Al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) Finally, Hashr Maidan is a place of great suffering. On the day receiving the intercession of the Prophet (Sm.) will be the greatest success. So, it is essential to do good deeds for everyone to get intercession.\n---"}]

question: Tasin, a student of class 10, visited Haringhata tourist center with his cousin during winter vacation this year. He was overwhelmed to see the blue waters of the sea from the tourist tower surrounded by green, forests near the Bay of Bengal. Unknowingly came out of his mind, how beautifully the Almighty has made the sea. Cousin Tamim said this world of creation was created naturally.What is the mercy of God here?
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is human values?","marks":1,"answer":"Human values encompass actions, thoughts, and ideas that align with human beings and civilization."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"\"I have not left anything out in this book.\" — Explain this verse of Allah.","marks":2,"answer":"\"I have not left anything out in this book\" the verse declares the completeness of the Qur'an. The Qur'an stands as an irrefutable and authentic document of Shariah. It contains a clear description of all aspects and sections of human life. In this book, Allah Ta'ala has outlined clear principles and instructions for managing human life, devoid of ambiguity, distortion, or complexity. Hence, Allah Ta'ala asserts, \"I have not left anything out in this book\" (Surah Al-Anam, Ayat: 38)."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain that aspect in the light of Islamic shariah which is shown in the statement of Tamim.","marks":3,"answer":"Tamim's statement exhibit Kufr. Kufr denotes denial or disbelief. In Islamic terminology, disbelief in any of the fundamental principles of Islam is termed as kufr. Individuals can engage in kufr in various ways. For instance, disbelief in the existence of Allah, disbelief in the attributes of Allah, or considering haram as halal, etc., which is noticeable in Tamim. In the aforementioned context, Tamim asserts that the universe is naturally created, devoid of mercy from Allah. Tamim's viewpoint constitutes kufr because it entails denying the attributes of Allah Ta'ala. Refusing to acknowledge Allah Ta'ala as the Creator or Sustainer equates to denying His attributes, thus constituting kufr. Hence, it can be asserted that Tamim has committed Kufr by rejecting Allah Ta'ala as the ruler of the world."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the rationale of Tasin's statement in the light of textbook.","marks":4,"answer":"Tawhid is identified in the statement of Tasin. Tawhid is the acceptance of Allah Ta'ala as One and Unique. He is the sole ruler and owner of this universe, having no partners. He is unique and incomparable, with signs of His presence evident throughout the universe. If one examines the creations of the world, including planets, stars, the moon, and the sun, signs of the oneness of Allah Almighty are observed, as revealed in Tamim's activities. In the above scenario, \"Tawhid or the monotheism of Allah is expressed in Tasin's statement. Indeed, Allah is the creator of everything. What a beautiful world we live in, with rivers, streams, seas, oceans, mountains, etc. These are not created by themselves. The one who masterfully created and manages these things is Allah the Exalted. If there were more than one creator in this vast universe, then the universe would not be managed in an orderly manner. Various kinds of chaos would have appeared, or this universe would have been destroyed by now. This implies that Allah Almighty is one, unique, and incomparable. Finally, it can be concluded that Allah created everything. He owns everything. Since this belief is expressed in Tasin's statement, his faith belongs to the stage of Tawhid.\n---"}]

subject: Islamic And Moral Studies
question: 'B' is a grocer. Side by side, he gives loan to the people for certain time and takes return with some extra amount. His mother told him, "Such transaction is Haram". He replied, "Almost, all financial institution run with this system. So, it is Halal." Mother said again, "You have to give the account of all these activities to Allah and have to suffer for those activities. Your father would rear up such faith and led his whole life in the path of truth and justice."
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What does 'Risalat' mean?","marks":1,"answer":"The responsibility of conveying the Holy Message of Almighty Allah to people is called Risalat."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"\"There is nothing that resembles Him.\" — Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The Ayat in question is from Surah Ash-Shura. Believe in Akhirat keeps man away from wrong deeds and encourages to do good deeds. This is seen in the actions of B’s father. In the passage, Mr. B’s mother said about his father that “One must give the account of all the wrong deeds in front of Allah. Your father believes that and that is why he lived his whole life honestly.” His father did this because of his fear of Akhirat. For a man believing in Akhirat knows that he will have to stand before Allah in Akhirat and account for all his deeds on earth. As a result, a man believing in Akhirat is inspired towards good deeds and refrains himself from evil deeds. Thus, a man shuns bad conduct and acquires good manners. On the other hand, he who disbelieves in Akhirat, indulges in sin and indecent activities in the first chance available. For he does not have faith in accountability in the next life. A man believing in Akhirat cannot ever indulge in sinful and obscene acts. At last it can be said that because Mr. B’s father believes in Akhirat, he spent his entire life in honesty. That is why his mother’s evaluation is correct. We should all believe in Akhirat and refrain ourselves from all kind of sinful deeds."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Do you think that the speech of 'B' contradictory to an important issue of Aqaid? Opine with logics.","marks":4,"answer":"Yes, the speech of 'B' contradicts the crucial matter of Aqaid with Iman, which is tantamount to Kufr. Kufr means to reject, disbelieve, and to be disobedient etc. In the Islamic parlance rejection or disbelief in any or one of the fundamental issues of Islam is Kufr. Believing that drinking wine, gambling, taking interest, indulging in bribery etc. are permitted, is also Kufr. This is seen in B’s mentality. In the passage, the mentality of Mr. B is similar to Kufr. This is an example of interest taking transaction. Allah has forbidden drinking wine, taking interest, taking bribe. When someone believes the forbidden things as permitted, they commit Kufr and become Kafir. The consequence of Kufr in human life is very grave. One will have to suffer dire consequences for Kufr not only in this life but also in the next life. They will stay in hell for eternity and suffer the painful punishment of hell. That is why it can be said that Kufr is seen in B’s mentality.\n---"}]

question:

parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Iman?","marks":1,"answer":"Iman is to belief in the laws and regulations of Islamic shariat at heart, to confess in words and to demonstrate in practice."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Describe the nature of Tawhid.","marks":2,"answer":"Tawhid is the first and most important aspect of Iman. But even though 4000 rupees were spent on the event, Adil says all the money has been spent. By doing this, he has betrayed the deposit. question: Son of Jalal is Jamal Uddin and he is affected by Covid-19. That is why Jalal slaughtered a cow in the name of his peer and he prays also to his peer for his son's recovery. question: Tazkia is a Muslim. She offers Salat regularly. But she mocks some issues of Islam. Being informed the matter, her teacher said, "Its consequences and demerits are very grave in here and hereafter life."
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Tawhid?","marks":1,"answer":"To acknowledge that Allah is One and only is called Tawhid."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the relationship between Iman and Islam.","marks":2,"answer":"The relationship between Iman and Islam are interrelated. Iman instills in human beings a sense of belief in Allah and the hope of getting his blessings. As a result, through worship and loyalty towards Allah, Islam flourishes. Islam is the external face of Iman. The faith in Allah is expressed through Islam and guides people towards welfare. People can indulge in kufr in many ways. For example, denying the existence and attributes of Allah, denying the fundamental worship of Islam, considering haram as halal and halal as haram, making fun of the Holy Prophet (Sm.) or the Quran, etc., are included in Kufr. Through these actions, people become infidels. Such a negative belief has emerged in Tazkia's behavior as well. In the above stem, Tazkia makes fun of important issues in Islam. Therefore, it can be said that the behavior of Tazkia is included in kufr as it makes fun of the important issues of Islam."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Evaluate the accuracy of teacher's comment mentioned in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"The consequences and demerits of kufr are very grave in here and after life\" this comment of the teacher mentioned in the stem is accurate. Making fun of any important matter of Islam, the chosen deen of Allah Ta'ala, is part of Kufr. Its consequences in human life are very dire. Not only in the world; Rather, in the Akhirat, as a result of this, people will have to suffer very dire consequences. Because disbelief creates disobedience and ingratitude in people. As a result, a Kafir person does not believe in Almighty Allah, the Hereafter, Prophets, etc., that is why he indulges in worldly pleasures, comforts and various wrongdoings. He does not believe in heaven and hell, so he does not care about the afterlife. As a result, worldly life prevails for him. So, for the sake of the world, he gets involved in misdeeds like lying, lawlessness, murder, robbery etc. As a result, immorality spread in the society. And for this she will have to suffer a terrible fate in the world and in the Akhirat. One of her teachers commented that Tazkia's behavior revealed disbelief. Tazkia from the above stem claims to be a Muslim and offers regular prayers. However, she has indulged in Kufr by making fun of important matters of Islam. And for the disbelievers there awaits a severe punishment in the Hereafter, the consequences of which are very dire. Because Allah Ta'ala says about the disbelievers, \"Those who disbelieve and reject our signs will surely abide in the hell. They will remain there forever.\" (Sura: Al-Baqara, Ayat: 39) Therefore, She should refrain from such actions and return to the path of Allah with proper repentance. Otherwise, she will have to face severe punishment in the Akhirat.\n---"}]

question:
Scenario-1: Hanif is an intelligent student. One day he said to his teacher that all schools have one head teacher. Why is there not more than one head teacher in any school? His teacher said that if any school has more than on head teacher, the discipline will be destroyed in the activities of the school.
Scenario-2: One day Manif went to visit a historical place with his father. They noticed there that some people were praying in prostration at the grave of a great man. His father said, "It is a grave sin."
parts: [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Kufr?","marks":1,"answer":"Disbelief in any of the fundamentals of Islam is referred to as kufr."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"\"The Munafiq's are harmful than the Kafirs\". — Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The munafiqs, who are the secret enemies, pose a greater threat to Islam than the kafirs, who are the obvious enemies. Those who conceal disbelief and disobedience in their hearts while professing Islam verbally are Munafiqs. They are more detrimental to Islam and Muslims than infidels because they associate with Muslims while aiding the kafirs, who are enemies of Islam. They expose the secrets and vulnerabilities of Muslims to the infidels, constantly engaging in harming Muslims. However, Muslims fail to grasp this reality. Therefore, hidden enemy hypocrites are more detrimental to Islam than open enemy kafirs."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Which matter of Islam has similarity with the fact exposed in the conversation between Hanif and his teacher in scenario-1? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The conversation in scenario-1 between Hanif and his teacher has similarities with the main aspect of Islam, Tawhid, i.e., the Oneness of Allah. The word Tawhid means monotheism. Acknowledging Allah Ta'ala as One and Unique is called Tawhid. Tawhid is the belief in Allah Ta'ala as the Creator, Sustainer, and the One and only Being worthy of worship. Belief in Tawhid is the key to Iman. No person can enter Islam without belief in Tawhid. The discussion of this topic is also noteworthy in the above scenario. In scenario-1 from the above context, the importance of the Oneness of Almighty Allah is observed in the conversation between Hanif and his teacher. Because if there is more than one head teacher in the school, all the activities and discipline of the school will be destroyed. In the same way, if there were any creator other than Almighty Allah in the universe, there would be chaos. Because if there were any other god besides Allah, then there would be no order in the activities of this world and the heavens. Not everything would be so well managed. In scenario-1 of the context, Hanif and his teacher have a conversation about this monotheism of Allah."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Evaluate the accuracy of Manif's father's statement in scenario-2 in light of Islam.","marks":4,"answer":"A 'Shirk is a very heinous crime' - the statement of Manif's father in scenario-2 is accurate in the light of Islam. In scenario-2, one day Manif went to visit a historical place with his father. There they saw some people prostrating at the grave of a great man and praying. Then his father said to him, 'This is a very heinous crime.' Because Shirk is the greatest of all types of oppression in the world. Allah Ta'ala says, 'Verily, shirk is the extreme tyranny.' (Surah Luqman, verse 13) And indeed, Shirk is an unforgivable crime. Allah Ta'ala is very displeased with the polytheists. He does not forgive the crime of shirk, despite being extremely forgiving. Allah says, 'Surely, Allah will not forgive the sin of Shirk. Besides Shirk, He may forgive any other sin of whom He so desires.' (Surah An-Nisa, Ayat 48) Finally, it can be said that to join the worship of Allah by prostrating at the grave of a great person is included in Shirk, which is a very heinous crime. And we must always stay away from such a heinous crime, i.e., Shirk.\n---"}]
